 SINGAPORE: The air quality across Singapore is expected to continue being in the moderate band on Wednesday (Oct 27), the National Environment Agency (NEA) said on Tuesday.
 The 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) forecast for Wednesday is between 60 to 90. 
 Winds are forecast to blow from the east-northeast on Wednesday, NEA said in its evening advisory.  
 "Showers are expected over Kalimantan, Sumatra and Singapore and surrounding region which could continue to help with the haze situation," it added.

 For Thursday and Friday, winds are expected to blow from the east-southeast or south-southeast.
 "While this could transport smoke haze from southern Sumatra, showers are forecast over the region which should help to lower the risk of haze," NEA said.
 Air quality was moderate across Singapore on Tuesday afternoon, with the 24-hour Pollutant Standard Index (PSI) ranging from 62 to 75 at 7pm.
 Hourly PM2.5 levels in the northern region returned to the normal band, with a reading of 26, after entering the elevated range at 4pm. 
 PM2.5 readings in the other regions remained within the normal band, ranging from 21 to 34.
 Air quality across Singapore has remained in the good-to-moderate range since 11pm on Sunday.
 NEA has advised the public to refer to the 24-hour PSI forecast when planning outdoor activities and to check the latest 1-hour PM2.5 readings before undertaking immediate outdoor activities.
 Based on the 24-hour PSI forecast for Tuesday, all individuals can engage in outdoor activities as usual.
 When hourly PM2.5 concentrations are in the elevated band, healthy individuals should reduce strenuous outdoor activities for the next hour.
 Vulnerable groups, including children, elderly people, pregnant women and those with chronic heart or lung conditions, should avoid strenuous outdoor activities during that period.
